source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Seed corn maggot (ដង្កូវចោះគ្រាប់ពោត, Seed Corn Maggot): this is a fly whose larvae damage corn seed by boring into and hollowing it out. The larvae are legless and yellowish/creamy in color. This pest is especially problematic in fields where there is a large amount of decomposing organic residue in the soil, such as fields recently planted with beans/legumes before corn -- corn planted as a follow-on crop after beans is at particular risk because the maggots are attracted to decaying plant material in the soil, which favors their build-up in the field.

Prevention and control measures:
- Select suitable, clean, treated seed for planting.
- Plant according to the appropriate time of year.
- Clear crop debris that is present in the field, especially residue left near where clean seed lots have been kept, particularly leftover residue of related crop types.
- Collect maggots and destroy them by burning.
- Ensure the field has good drainage before planting so water does not sit around the seed.
